precepts.point: Now I'm going to show you what Esau doing concerning that. No, I wanted to go to Esther 2 and 12, but I ain't going to go there. You all go there and read it about purification. It tell you Esther did purification in incense and so forth, and everything else she need, and she had a maid and all of that to help her and so forth. You know what I mean? So purification is also, you know, is a lot of stuff. It's also food, you know, the things she need, food, all of that, you know.

note.label: The Decayed State of Liberal Women

precepts.why:
Leviticus 12:4 says “she shall touch no hallowed thing, nor come into the sanctuary, until the days of her purifying be fulfilled.” Purification means being washed, cleansed, made holy; literally, removing what is foreign and contaminated to restore something to its natural clean state. So purification is not just staying away from the temple. The days of her separation are also her being nursed back to health, restored.

Esther shows purification too. Go there and read it for yourselves: Esther went through her days of purification with sweet odours and so forth, and everything else she needed, and she had maids to help her. It is a different purification, but it shows that purifying a woman is a lot of stuff: care, help, the right food, the things her body needs.

So it is with a woman after she gives birth. She was not just sent home and left alone. For those forty days, or eighty for a girl, she was kept in a special place, and midwives and family came, cooked the right food and nursed her back to health. That is postpartum in the Bible, and it is why a sister who has just given birth needs people around her and help with the baby, not the postpartum depression that Esau made up.

precepts.text: There was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, a mighty man of power; and he had a son, whose name was Saul. So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows.
precepts.point: Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite: Mordecai and Esther were of the tribe of Benjamin.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

precepts.why:
Esther 2:5 gives Mordecai’s line: “a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Mordecai, and Esther with him, were of the tribe of Benjamin. Go back to 1 Samuel 9 and see who Kish is.

“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Kish was a mighty man of power.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.”

So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line, the line of Kish. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows, because the enemy Saul was sent against in his day, the Amalekites and their king Agag, shows up again in Mordecai’s day. The hatred is perpetual, and it runs down the same lines.

precepts.text: There is a difference between a wife and a virgin, the unmarried woman being the virgin who cares for the things of the Lord, not a child.
precepts.point: Fair young virgins here does not mean little girls but women of marital age, and the maiden who pleased the king would be made queen instead of Vashti, and the thing pleased the king.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

precepts.why:
The king's servants counsel “Let there be fair young virgins sought for the king”, gathered “unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women”, and “let the maiden which pleaseth the king be queen instead of Vashti.” Fair young virgins does not mean little girls. These are women of marital age, one of whom is to be queen.

Paul shows what a virgin is in scripture: “There is difference also between a wife and a virgin. The unmarried woman careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and in spirit: but she that is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.” The virgin is the unmarried woman, set beside the wife, not a child. She is a woman who has not yet married and so careth for the things of the Lord; when she marries, she careth how she may please her husband.

So the virgins gathered to the house of the women were unmarried women, and the maiden who pleased the king became his wife and queen.

precepts.text: Seek the peace of the city where you are carried away captive and pray for it, for in its peace you shall have peace, which is why Mordecai kept the king safe.
precepts.point: The thing was known to Mordecai who told it to Esther the queen, and Esther told the king in Mordecai's name, and when it was searched out and found true the two were both hanged on a tree, and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king. Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai's would later help our whole nation.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

precepts.why:
Two of the king's chamberlains “were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus”, plotting a coup, and “the thing was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.” Mordecai was a captive in Persia, yet he kept the king safe.

That is what the Lord had told the captives to do: “seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the Lord for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.” The Lord caused them to be carried there; a coup against the king was no peace for the city, and no peace for Israel in it. So Mordecai exposed it.

“when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.” Israel wrote down our history and our chronicles, and this deed of Mordecai's, written in the king's book, would later help our whole nation. In the peace of the city, Israel had peace.

precepts.text: The canonical book names the same Mardocheus, a Benjamite carried away from Jerusalem with Jeconiah by Nebuchadnezzar, the very account the Apocrypha references.
precepts.point: Mardocheus was one of the captives whom Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon carried from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea. This same captivity and lineage are named in the canonical book, which proves the Apocrypha runs right along with the rest of the Bible.

note.label: Esther 11: The Dream of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
Mardocheus is set out by his line and his captivity: “Mardocheus the son of Jairus, the son of Semei, the son of Cisai, of the tribe of Benjamin”, a Jew who “dwelt in the city of Susa, a great man, being a servitor in the king’s court”, and “one of the captives, which Nabuchodonosor the king of Babylon carried from Jerusalem with Jechonias king of Judea”.

The canonical book names the same man the same way: “Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite; Who had been carried away from Jerusalem with the captivity which had been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon had carried away.” Jairus is Jair, Semei is Shimei, Cisai is Kish; Susa is Shushan, Jechonias is Jeconiah, Nabuchodonosor is Nebuchadnezzar. One Benjamite, one captivity, one account.

That is the proof that the Apocrypha runs right along with the rest of the Bible. The dream of Mardocheus is not a story off to the side; it references the very captivity and lineage the canonical book records.

precepts.text: The canonical book records the same two chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, who sought to lay hands on the king, whom Mardocheus exposed through Esther, and who were both hanged on a tree.
precepts.point: This is the same account found in Esther chapter 2, where Mardocheus sat in the king's gate, uncovered the plot of the two chamberlains, and told it through Esther the queen. The king examined the two eunuchs, and after they confessed, they were strangled.

note.label: Esther 12: Mardocheus Uncovers the Plot and Aman's Hatred

precepts.why:
Mardocheus “took his rest in the court with Gabatha and Tharra, the two eunuchs of the king, and keepers of the palace.” He “heard their devices, and searched out their purposes, and learned that they were about to lay hands upon Artexerxes the king; and so he certified the king of them.” The king examined the two eunuchs, “and after that they had confessed it, they were strangled.”

This is the same account found in the canonical book. “In those days, while Mordecai sat in the king’s gate, two of the king’s chamberlains, Bigthan and Teresh, of those which kept the door, were wroth, and sought to lay hand on the king Ahasuerus.” Gabatha and Tharra are Bigthan and Teresh, the keepers of the palace who kept the door. The thing “was known to Mordecai, who told it unto Esther the queen; and Esther certified the king thereof in Mordecai’s name.” He told it through Esther the queen, and the king was certified of it in his name.

“And when inquisition was made of the matter, it was found out; therefore they were both hanged on a tree: and it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.” The king examined them, it was found out, and the two died for it. The Apocrypha and the canonical book are telling one story from two sides.

points: Esther had not shown her people nor her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to show it, and Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women's house to know how Esther did. note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: Every maid's turn to go in to the king came after twelve months of purification, six months with oil of myrrh and six months with sweet odours and other things for the purifying of the women. Israel kept such a season of preparing, and our women always smelled good.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: She went in the evening and returned to the second house of the women under the keeper of the concubines, and came in unto the king no more except he delighted in her and called her by name. The king had houses set aside for his concubines, for he was the king of Persia and not an Israelite.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

points: When Esther's turn came, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai who took her for his daughter, she required nothing but what Hegai the keeper of the women appointed, and Esther obtained favour in the sight of all who looked upon her.

note.label: Esther 2: Esther Made Queen and Mordecai Uncovers the Plot

Esther was chosen above all the women, for that is what a daughter of Israel is.
